glossary.Pleuritic: Sharp chest pain made worse by breathing in or coughing.
glossary.Fibrous sac: A tough bag of connective tissue, here the pericardium wrapping the heart.
glossary.Tachycardia: A fast heart rate, over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Malar rash: A red butterfly-shaped rash over the cheeks and nose, typical of SLE.
glossary.Synovitis: Inflammation of the lining of a joint.
glossary.Pacemaker: A device implanted under the skin that sends electrical pulses to keep the heart beating regularly.
glossary.Anticoagulation: Treatment that thins the blood to stop clots forming.
glossary.Diastolic filling: The filling of the ventricles with blood while the heart relaxes.
glossary.Ascites: Fluid build-up in the abdominal cavity.
glossary.Right HF: Right-sided heart failure: fluid backs up into the body, causing raised JVP, oedema and liver swelling.
glossary.EBV: Epstein-Barr virus, the cause of glandular fever.
glossary.HIV: Human immunodeficiency virus, which attacks the immune system.
glossary.VZV: Varicella zoster virus, the cause of chickenpox and shingles.
glossary.Echo 8: Echovirus type 8, an enterovirus that can cause pericarditis.
glossary.CKD: Chronic kidney disease: long-term loss of kidney function.
glossary.Uraemic: Caused by a build-up of urea and waste in the blood from kidney failure.
glossary.Troponin: A heart muscle protein released into the blood when heart cells are damaged.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein, a blood marker that rises with inflammation or infection.
glossary.ST elevation: Raised ST segment on the ECG, seen in heart attack or pericarditis.
glossary.T-P segment: The flat part of the ECG between the end of the T wave and the next P wave.
glossary.QRS: The ECG spike showing the ventricles contracting.
glossary.Peptic ulcer disease: Sores in the lining of the stomach or duodenum, made worse by NSAIDs.
glossary.Xiphoid: The small pointed bottom tip of the breastbone.
glossary.Pneumothorax: Air in the space around the lung, causing it to collapse.
glossary.Melanoma: A cancer of the pigment cells of the skin that often spreads.
glossary.Neoplastic: Caused by a tumour or cancer.
glossary.Haemodialysis: Filtering the blood through a machine when the kidneys fail.
glossary.Diuretics: Drugs that make the kidneys remove more salt and water.
glossary.Visceral pericardium: The inner layer of the pericardium stuck to the heart's surface.
glossary.Parietal pericardium: The outer layer of the pericardium, lining the fibrous sac.
glossary.Intrapericardial pressure: The pressure inside the pericardial sac around the heart.
glossary.Cardiac output: The amount of blood the heart pumps per minute.
glossary.Electrical axis: The overall direction of the heart's electrical activity seen on ECG.
glossary.MI: Myocardial infarction: a heart attack from a blocked coronary artery.
glossary.Autoimmune disease: A condition in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Raised JVP: A higher than normal jugular venous pressure in the neck, showing high right-sided filling pressure.
